title: Walsh-Zero Vector Spaces in 3-Round Feistel Networks
summary: Several families of vector spaces are known, and their count is unexpectedly large for 8-bit permutations; explaining this abundance remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a 3-round Feistel network $F$ that is a permutation on an 8-bit domain, explain why the Walsh-zero set $\mathcal{Z}_F$ contains so many vector spaces.

scope.domain: Structural questions in symmetric cryptanalysis about Walsh-zero sets and vector spaces of Feistel permutations.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Explain why the Walsh-zero set contains so many vector spaces for the stated construction and domain.

citations.label: Anomalies and Vector Space Search: Tools for S-Box Analysis

progress.summary: The paper lists this as Open Problem 2 after presenting several families of vector spaces in the Walsh zeroes of 3-round Feistel networks. It observes that the number is unexpectedly large for 8-bit permutations but does not explain the phenomenon.
citation_labels: Xavier Bonnetain et al., Anomalies and Vector Space Search: Tools for S-Box Analysis
